gaps.name: merge-pipeline-gaps-md-regenerated-on-land
gaps.title: The entries move to the records and the merge queue writes docs/GAPS.md from them inside each landing; every reader still reads GAPS.md
gaps.definition: Problem: the entries must move to dev/records/ without a window in which a branch's GAPS.md edit is read by nothing or overwritten. So the writing is cut over first and the readers later: after this gap GAPS.md is always the render of the records, and every reader (intake, deps, brief, plan, knowledge) still reads it, unchanged. Change: (1) run `gapsdoc.py split` once and commit it: each entry appended as `## Entry` at the end of dev/records/<branch>.md, never overwriting, head to dev/records/GAPS-head.md; GAPS.md itself does not change in that commit. (2) Old definitions stay findable: fac.definition_file (dev/bin/fac.py:224-233) counts dev/records/<branch>.md as the definition only when it has a `## Definition of done` section, otherwise it returns docs/roadmap/overnight/<branch>.md when that exists; implement.definition_first (implement.py:44-58) appends to an Entry-only record and never writes a second definition for a gap whose old-folder file exists. (3) queue.py renders inside the landing: after land() returns and before the point of no return (before `done = True`, the saved `landing` state and gap.merged, queue.py:835-842), it first carries the batch's own GAPS.md edits into the records (gapsdoc.carry(pre, head): entry text and done lines the batch added to GAPS.md that the records lack are appended to the named records and said by name; one it cannot place is said on the run as `gaps_md_unplaced` and kept in dev/records/GAPS-unplaced.md, never dropped), then renders and commits a differing result as `docs/GAPS.md from the records`; `merged` is reassigned to that commit, so main_sha on every landed gap and the sha ask() pushes are the same head, and recover() treats it as part of the landing. A render failure lands the batch without the commit and says `gaps_md: why` on the run, never blocking a merge. (4) implement.py refuses, uncounted and before the suites (next to strays, implement.py:228-231), a branch whose own new commits touch docs/GAPS.md, with a brief pointing at the record's Entry; branches already approved are carried by (3). house-rules.md:33-34 and dev/README.md say the entry is written in the record. The union merge stays until merge-pipeline-gaps-md-edits-retired. Done: intake and deps give the same gaps, closes, links and sources after the migration commit as before it; an approved branch that edited GAPS.md lands and its text is in a record and on the pushed head; main_sha equals the pushed sha (tested); no record change makes no commit; a malformed record lands the batch and leaves GAPS.md as it was; a gap defined only in the old folder still resolves to that file after the split (tested for a continued gap's REF too); a new GAPS.md edit is refused uncounted. Files: dev/bin/queue.py, dev/bin/gapsdoc.py, dev/bin/implement.py, dev/bin/fac.py, dev/records/, dev/knowledge/house-rules.md, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py, tests/test_gapsdoc.py. gaps.name: merge-pipeline-stacks-land-bottom-up
gaps.title: The merge queue lands a stacked gap only with or after its base, and never without it
gaps.definition: Problem: a stacked branch holds its base's reviewed commits, but picks() (queue.py:505-558) and land() (queue.py:635-729) see only each gap's own reviewed commit: taken alone it would land its base's work under its own name, and in a red batch a descendant re-merged onto the green prefix (queue.py:718-722) would bring the failing commit back. Change, reading the field `stacked_on: [{gap, sha}]`: picks() brings an unmerged base in below its dependent, bottom-up and recursively, and only at the sha the dependent holds: a base whose reviewed head is not that sha gives the dependent back uncounted (it waits for merge-forward); a base not approved, held by a run, or a stack over the batch cap gives the run's own gap back uncounted (after 10m, never towards EMPTY_MOST, queue.py:561-580); a stacked batch-mate whose base cannot come is skipped. land(): when a merge is blamed, every later merge whose stacked_on reaches it at any depth goes back to approved uncounted and is never re-merged. Done: A then B land in one batch; B with A in fix is given back with the reason; B holding an older sha of A than A's reviewed head is given back and A lands alone; A failing gives B back and the pushed tree holds neither; a stack of 3 with cap 2 gives the own gap back; a batch with no stacked gap behaves exactly as today (pinned). Files: dev/bin/queue.py, tests/test_factory.py. Budget: 95 net lines in dev/bin.

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-bisect-in-parallel-rounds
gaps.title: A red batch finds every failing merge in parallel rounds of its named tests, then lands on one full run
gaps.definition: Problem: after each failing merge land() starts a new full run of 9 to 13 minutes on the rest (queue.py:718-722), and a ruff failure bisects with full runs of every suite (queue.py:698). Change: in land(), a red run whose named tests fail alone on the red tree (and are not main's, per bisect-tests-main-itself) is bisected in rounds: run the named tests on every prefix at once (prefixes.run_all); the first failing prefix's last merge is blamed and given to triage as now, with its stacked descendants; rebuild the survivors and repeat until the names pass; then one full run on the survivors (red with new names starts again). Ruff is bisected the same way per prefix. An unknown prefix result makes that round serial; the time allowance (Late) is checked before each round; batch_rounds and prefix_runs go on suites_queue. Done: 8 with one bad merge costs one full run, one named run, the main check, one parallel round and one full run on the 7; two bad merges take two rounds and one final full run; ruff found in one round; unknown never counts as pass; docstring says an interaction failure blames the later merge. Files: dev/bin/queue.py, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py. Budget: 120 net lines in dev/bin.

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-relation-starts-at
gaps.title: A precedence relation may name the target states at which a dependent may start
gaps.definition: Problem: precedence is finish-to-start only (ergostat/precedence.py:93-105; ergostat/leases/ready.py:75-84), so a dependent waits for its target to finish though work could start once the target is, say, approved. Engine part only; the factory does not use it yet. Change: a relation's map form takes `starts_at: [STATE, ...]`, states of the target kind (ergostat/spec/relations.py REL_KEYS, the Relation IR); a target in one of them does not block `takes: {unblocked: true}` or precedence status. CPM and the schedule stay finish-to-start (said in docstring and SPEC). check refuses a state the target kind lacks, starts_at on a non-precedence relation, and a finished or paused state named. The item index and Items API expose it. Done: a gap whose only dependency is approved is taken with `starts_at: [approved]`, not with the dependency in fix; the critical path still waits for the finish; one finding per refusal with a stated code; SPEC §5a and §9.5 and schema/ergostat.schema.json updated. Files: ergostat/spec/relations.py, ergostat/spec/ir.py, ergostat/precedence.py, ergostat/leases/ready.py, schema, docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_relations.py, tests/test_precedence.py. Budget: 90 net lines.

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-stacked-gap-builds-on-its-base
gaps.title: A gap whose dependencies are approved is built on their reviewed branches, not on main
gaps.definition: Problem: agents.clone always branches from origin/main (agents.py:282-296) and implement.py measures and merges against main (implement.py:200, 202, 227, 228, 238, 244), so a gap cannot start until its dependencies merged. Inert until stacks-turned-on. Change: fac.stack_base(cfg, gap) returns the reviewed heads ({gap, sha}, rank order) of a gap whose unfinished dependencies are each approved, queued or push-pending, else none. With bases, implement.py clones as now and merges each base's reviewed head (`--no-ff`, never a rebase or squash), records `stacked_on` on gap.started and gap.built, uses the merge of main and every base (a commit under refs/stack/<branch>) as the base for strays, net_lines, check findings and onmain, and has finish hold each base sha. Bases that conflict with each other give the gap back uncounted naming files. A base whose reviewed head moved after the gap started is not a give-back loop: a gap not yet started simply takes the new head, and a started gap keeps building on the sha it holds and waits for merge-forward (merge-pipeline-stacks-merged-forward) to carry the new one. Done: net_lines and strays count only the gap's own commits; two conflicting bases give back uncounted naming files; stacked_on is on the item; finish refuses a head missing a base sha; a fix round on a gap whose base moved still builds (on the held sha); an unstacked gap builds exactly as today (pinned). Files: dev/bin/fac.py, dev/bin/implement.py, dev/bin/agents.py, tests/test_factory.py. Budget: 130 net lines in dev/bin.

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-stacks-merged-forward
gaps.title: When a stacked gap's base moves, the new base is merged forward into it; a conflict goes back to its implementor
gaps.definition: Problem: a base can change after its descendant started (back to fix and approved at a new head); the descendant still holds the old reviewed sha and nothing carries the new commits forward. The owner's direction is merge forward, never rebase or squash. Change: new dev/bin/stack.py run as a block stack-forward in dev/model/building.yaml (every 5m, commanded by a sensor counting stale stacks). For each gap whose base's reviewed head moved and is approved again (or landed: only update stacked_on): skip if leased, building or in review; else merge the new base head into the branch in a scratch clone (`--no-ff`) and move the drop's branch from its old tip only. Clean on an approved gap: record the new reviewed_head with `reviewed_by: stack-forward` and stacked_on. Clean on built or fix: move the branch. Conflict: abort, send to fix with the files (`stack_conflict`), uncounted. Bottom-up, so a stack of three moves in one pass. Done: those four cases, a drop branch that moved during the merge is refused (theirs kept), block and sensor in the model with no new check finding. Files: dev/bin/stack.py (new), dev/model/building.yaml, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py. Budget: 150 net lines in dev/bin.

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-stacks-turned-on
gaps.title: Stacking turned on: gaps start on approved dependencies, reviewed against their base
gaps.definition: Problem: with the engine option, the implementor, the queue and merge-forward ready, the factory still waits for merges: ergostat.yaml:115 declares depends_on finish-to-start, the reviewer diffs against main (review.py:182-187) so a stacked gap would be sized with its base's lines, and deps.blocked_reason (deps.py:165-166) says it waits. It is turned on only after merge-forward exists, because without it a base reworked to a new head would strand every gap stacked on it. Change: ergostat.yaml `depends_on: {kind: gap, starts_at: [approved, queued, push-pending]}`; review.py uses fac.stack_base's merged base (refs/stack/<branch>) for the diff, net_lines and gate 1's main check, and the brief names the bases; deps.py says `stacked on X (approved)`; dev/model/building.yaml gains a stock gaps-stacked; dev/README.md gains a section Stacked gaps (built, reviewed, landed, and what happens when a base fails, moves or parks). Done: on a copy of the factory's model a ready gap whose only dependency is approved is taken; the reviewer gets only the gap's own diff and its net lines match the implementor's; a base sent to fix and approved at a new head is merged forward and the descendant then lands (one test through all four pieces); the Items page shows stacked on (no new UI); `ergostat check` adds no finding. Files: ergostat.yaml, dev/bin/review.py, dev/bin/deps.py, dev/model/building.yaml, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py, tests/test_backlog.py. Budget: 60 net lines.

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-browser-daily-on-main
gaps.title: Once a day the browser suite runs on main; a flake is recorded, a real failure is a test broken on main
gaps.definition: Problem: the owner wants the browser suite on a trigger rather than in every batch; that needs a safety net for changes outside its paths, and nothing runs the suite on main by itself (queue.py:156 is the only run). Change: new dev/bin/browserday.py run as a block browser-daily in dev/model/landing.yaml (every 24h), under the queue's lock (fac.queue_lock) after fac.wait_quiet, in a detached worktree at origin/main made and removed by name. Green: write {sha, at} to run/browser-daily.json. Red: rerun each named test alone twice (`-rA`). Every flake event goes through flakes.say, the one writer regression-flake-writes-hold-state makes: passing both reruns is flake.seen; the rest are tests broken on main, written as flake.main-broken with main's sha and, through onmain.record's intervention (dev/bin/onmain.py:89-97, one per main commit, class main-broken), the first-parent merges since the last green sha as suspects. There is no second representation of a broken main: the main-failing-tests stock and main-green goal of regression-guarantees-model see these items, and main-mend clears them. No names in the log: one intervention of class queue with the tail. A sensor browser-daily-age (hours since the last finished run, green or red; no reading when the file cannot be read) with a goal browser-daily-ran (<= 30, on-stale off, served by the block's own schedule and factory-off) says the net itself is alive; no new page. Done: green records the sha and the next day still runs; a flake raises nothing but flake.seen; a real failure is a main-broken item naming test and suspects; no flake event is written outside flakes.say; the lock is held; worktree and containers removed on every way out; no new check finding; README says so. Files: dev/bin/browserday.py (new), dev/bin/onmain.py (record takes suspects), dev/model/landing.yaml, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py. Budget: 150 net lines in dev/bin.

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-browser-only-on-its-paths
gaps.title: A batch skips the browser suite only when everything it touches is known not to reach the pages
gaps.definition: Problem: every queue run, each bisect step included, runs the four browser files (queue.py:156; factory.toml:170), about 9-10 minutes of 4 CPUs, though many batches change nothing a page reads. A list of paths that do reach the pages cannot be kept right by hand: ergostat/web/server.py imports ergostat/graph.py, model.py, history.py, series.py and state.py, and the diagrams come from ergostat/blockdiagram.py, dynamics.py, process.py and ergostat/spec/. So the rule is the safe way round: run the suite unless every changed path is on a list known not to reach it. Change: `[suites] browser_skips` in dev/factory.toml (default dev/bin/**, dev/prompts/**, dev/knowledge/**, dev/records/**, dev/factory.toml, docs/** but not docs/screenshots/**, *.md, and tests/test_*.py other than the browser files). Nothing under ergostat/, examples/, dev/model/, ergostat.yaml, tests/fixtures/, tests/conftest.py or scripts/ is skippable by default. queue.suites skips the browser step only when every path of `git diff --name-only pre HEAD` matches; then it records `browser: {not_run: "no path that reaches the pages changed"}` on suites_queue. rest() (queue.py:230-232) and excused() treat a not-run suite as finished, never stopped. An empty list runs browser always. Bisect sub-runs use the batch's decision. A config test walks the import closure of ergostat.web.server and of the four browser test files (ast, no import run) and fails if any module or fixture in it matches a skip pattern. Done: a dev/bin-only batch skips and says so; a batch touching ergostat/blockdiagram.py or dev/model/ runs it; an unlisted new path runs it; docstring and README name the daily run as the net. Files: dev/bin/queue.py, dev/factory.toml, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py. Budget: 40 net lines in dev/bin.

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-explain-remote-parts
gaps.title: explain names a remote's parts and the loops that cross into a remote
gaps.definition: Problem: remote-systems.md §6 says explain names the remote parts on a loop, but ergostat/spec/explain.py:141-157 lists loops with no remote marking and a part's or system's explanation (explain.py:389, :495) never says a part is a remote's, though AGENT-GUIDE §3a tells agents to explain before referencing. remote_of and box (ergostat/remote/__init__.py:9, :61) already know. gaps.title: User stories are items: story/A1..H6 synced from docs/roadmap/stories.md, owned by the design system
gaps.definition: Problem: the 46 stories measure whether a newcomer can use ergostat, but the factory knows them only as a markdown file walked by documentation-only gaps in the gap queue, the wrong queue by the owner's rule of one queue per kind of work. Change: an item kind `story` in ergostat.yaml (ids story/<code>; states due, obvious, possible, impossible, not-yet, retired; events story.listed and story.due to due, one per verdict, story.retired; shown: section, title, audience, demo, url, done_when, baseline, walked_at, walked_sha, screenshots, gaps; relation gaps: gap). New dev/bin/stories.py `sync` (program block, every 10 minutes) parses docs/roadmap/stories.md on main (each ### heading with its As, Demo and Done-when bullets, the demo from the URL's port through the Demos table), lists new stories, writes story.changed on a text change, retires removed ones. A system `design` within factory and dev/model/design.yaml: stocks stories-due, stories-obvious, stories-impossible, auxiliary stories-obvious-share, goal stories-obvious (share >= 0.8, tolerance 0.1; the 0.8 an estimate the owner sets). Done: a second sync writes nothing; a heading without a Demo line or with an unknown port refuses the sync by name, recording nothing; the model checks; dev/README.md gains 'The story queue'. Files: ergostat.yaml, dev/model/design.yaml, dev/bin/stories.py, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory_stories.py (five tests). Budget: 160 net lines.

gaps.name: research-design-queues-stories-due-after-merges
gaps.title: Stories become due again after a merge touches the page code or their demo, failing ones first
gaps.definition: Problem: a story is worth re-testing only when the page code or its demo changed, and nothing says when a story is stale. Cost is not the constraint: the factory's AI budget is $3000 a day (dev/model/budget.yaml:19) and a full sweep of 46 walks at $2 a session is $92, so no daily cap on walks is built; the designer block is paced by its pool of 1 and by goal.ai-budget.off (research-design-queues-designer-walks-stories). Change: `stories.py due`, a program block every 15 minutes in dev/model/design.yaml. A story not due and not retired is stale when `git diff --name-only walked_sha..main` touches ergostat/web/**, a module the pages render from (the same import closure of ergostat.web.server that merge-pipeline-browser-only-on-its-paths tests, computed here by a small shared helper if that gap has landed, else ergostat/** outside ergostat/compute/ and ergostat/library/run/), or examples/<its demo>/**, or when it was never walked. Every stale story is made due (story.due with why: the files and the merge), written in the order impossible, possible, not-yet, obvious, then oldest walk, so the designer, which takes the oldest due first, walks failing stories first. Model: a flow stories-made-due and a goal stories-walked (stories-due <= 0). Done: a merge touching ergostat/web/static/items.js makes stale stories due, failing first; a docs-only merge makes none due; a merge touching examples/the-job/ makes only that demo's stories due; the first run makes all never-walked stories due once; a second run with main unmoved writes nothing; an unreadable git state makes nothing due and exits non-zero. Files: dev/bin/stories.py, dev/model/design.yaml, tests/test_factory_stories.py (five tests). Budget: 70 net lines.

gaps.name: research-design-queues-designer-walks-stories
gaps.title: The designer queue: a session per due story starts its demo, walks it in a browser as a newcomer, and records a verdict with screenshots
gaps.definition: Problem: once stories are items nothing walks them; walks were done by hand outside the factory, so verdicts never reach the model, no stock moves and no goal is off. Change: a block `designer` (type ai, system design, pool 1, lease 60m, timeout 1h) in dev/model/design.yaml taking {kind: story, at: due, to: [obvious, possible, impossible, not-yet]}, driven by expr designer-when = goal.stories-walked.off * (1 - goal.ai-budget.off). New dev/bin/design.py clones main read-only, writes a brief from new dev/prompts/designer.md (the story's text, demo and URL, the newcomer rules, the owner's design decisions, the demo_up.py and walk.py commands with --shots /shots), runs one designer session, parses <walk verdict="obvious|possible|impossible|not-yet">steps, what was seen, why</walk>, copies /shots to run/stories/<story>-<n>/ and says story.<verdict> with walked_at, walked_sha, steps, why, screenshots and cost. No <walk> or an unknown verdict is a failed attempt (the lease retries once), never a verdict. The prompt: a newcomer who has not read the docs, stops at the story's bound, judges from screenshots, never edits. Done: the stand-in's verdict moves the story with screenshots copied; the block waits when the day's budget is spent; the item page lists screenshots and verdict history (fields only, no new UI); the model loads; README says how a walk runs. Files: dev/bin/design.py, dev/prompts/designer.md, dev/model/design.yaml, dev/bin/fac.py, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory_stories.py (four tests). Budget: 180 net lines.

gaps.name: research-design-queues-walk-findings-as-gaps
gaps.title: A walk that is not possible and obvious files its findings as small gaps, linked to the story, which is due again when they merge
gaps.definition: Problem: a verdict alone fixes nothing; the owner wants the designer queue to file findings as gaps, bounded so a sweep cannot flood the gap queue, never duplicated, and the story walked again when its gap merges. Change: under a non-obvious verdict the designer prompt asks for up to 3 <finding step="N" screenshot="name.png">one or two sentences</finding> tags outside code fences. design.py requests each as gap/story-<code>-<hash8 of the story and normalised finding>: title '<code>: <finding, cut>', source: story, size: S (no planner session), the story, the screenshot path, and a definition written by the program to run/defs/<branch>.md in the house shape (Problem with the done-when and screenshot, Change 'make this step possible and obvious within the owner's decisions', acceptance 'the story walked again passes this step', budget 80 lines). At most 3 per walk and `[design] gaps_per_day` (default 6, the bound on what a sweep may put in the gap queue, not a cost limit) per day from the record; an id that exists in any state is never requested again; each filed gap is added to the story's gaps. `stories.py due` also makes a story due when one of its gaps merges, written ahead of the other stale stories. Done: two findings file two S gaps linked on the story; the same finding next walk files nothing; five findings file 3 and note the rest; a fenced finding is ignored; README says so. Files: dev/bin/design.py, dev/bin/stories.py, dev/prompts/designer.md, dev/factory.toml, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory_stories.py (five tests). Budget: 130 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-runner-interface
gaps.title: A runner interface in the core, its first backend today's local runs
gaps.definition: Problem: a machine block's run reaches its process directly in five places (Engine._ran, ergostat/spec/engine.py:1060-1110; stop_run, :1855-1865; close, :1985-2001; the lease kill, ergostat/leases/kill.py:39-62; runner.LIVE and kill_all, ergostat/runner.py:38-59), so nothing but this machine can execute one (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 1). Order: the filed shard-supervisor also changes ergostat/runner.py and the engine's run handling, and this gap is a behaviour-preserving move whose done-when is that no test changes; so it is built after shard-supervisor has merged, on the code as that leaves it. Change: new ergostat/compute/runner.py with a Runner protocol (start(spec) -> Handle, follow, alive, kill(handle, why, grace), resources, cleanup) and `local`, today's code moved behind it unchanged; _ran, stop_run, close and leases/kill.py reach runs only through handles (eng.live maps run id to Handle); runner(spec, block) returns `local` always. Daemon runs stay as they are. No behaviour changes. Done: _ran holds no Measured, runrecord or stream call of its own; the records a run writes keep exactly their shape; the unit suite and the four browser files pass with no test edited except imports; SPEC §9.1 names the interface. Files: ergostat/compute/__init__.py, ergostat/compute/runner.py, ergostat/spec/engine.py, ergostat/leases/kill.py, tests/test_compute_runner.py (three tests), docs/SPEC.md. Full text: wave2-compute.md. Budget: 250 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-run-spec
gaps.title: A run as one JSON-able spec handed to its runner
gaps.definition: Problem: what a run is (command, input, cwd, environment, limits) is spread over local variables of _ran (ergostat/spec/engine.py:995-1059), so a backend on another machine can take none of it, and the engine's whole environment, every secret included, is in each run's. Change: ergostat/compute/spec.py, a RunSpec dataclass with to_json/from_json: run id, block, block type, command, input, cwd, env (only the ERGOSTAT_* variables _ran sets), secrets (names only), limits (wall from the block's timeout; the rest None unless given), work, out, lease (fence, ttl, expires). _ran builds one and passes it to runner.start. The local backend still runs with {**os.environ, **spec.env} (today's behaviour, said in a comment); allowlisted_env() returns PATH, HOME, LANG, the ERGOSTAT_* variables and the secrets named, for later backends. Run ids are checked against ^[0-9a-f]{32}$ for any backend but local. Done: exactly one RunSpec per run; a local run sees the same environment, input, cwd and command; it round-trips through JSON for program and ai blocks, leased, event-started and commanded; no secret value is a field. Files: ergostat/compute/spec.py, ergostat/compute/runner.py, ergostat/spec/engine.py, tests/test_compute_spec.py (four tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 180 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-pools-config
gaps.title: compute: pools in the model, with their check findings and ceilings
gaps.definition: Problem: a model cannot declare where runs may execute: there is no `compute:` section (ergostat/spec/compile.py:86-92; workspaces are the pattern, ergostat/workspaces/compile.py:15-41). This gap is the pools only; `runs-on:` on a block is compute-runs-on-config. Change: ergostat/compute/compile.py compiles `compute:` pools (nodes [{ssh: HOST} | {connect: [argv]}], backend process|docker, image, slots, limits {cpus, memory, pids, disk, wall, network, log}, repos, secrets {NAME: file}, labels) into a ComputePool in the IR (beside WorkspacePool, ir.py:503). Errors with their place: an unknown key; a bad size or duration; over 64 nodes or 64 slots; nodes x slots over 256 across pools; wall over a day; log over 1 GiB; `network: none` on the process backend; docker without image; a node entry naming an address or a user (`@` in ssh:). Nothing runs differently. Done: each refusal has its code; a model without compute: compiles to an identical IR; SPEC gains a compute: subsection. Files: ergostat/compute/compile.py, ergostat/spec/compile.py, ergostat/spec/ir.py, tests/test_compute_compile.py, docs/SPEC.md. Full text: wave2-compute.md (the pool half). Budget: 170 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-runs-on-config
gaps.title: runs-on: on a block names its pool, with the refusals for blocks that cannot run on a node
gaps.definition: Problem: with pools declared, a block still cannot say it runs on one: there is no `runs-on:` key. Change in ergostat/compute/compile.py and the block compiler: `runs-on: POOL|local` becomes Block.runs_on in the IR. Errors with their place: an unknown pool; runs-on on a daemon, sensor or ai block; runs-on on a command that uses calls (ERGOSTAT_CMD, ERGOSTAT_SOCKET, `ergostat `), until compute-calls-from-node lifts it; a pool used by blocks of two shards. Nothing runs differently yet: runner() still returns local. Done: each refusal has its code; a block with `runs-on: local` or none compiles to an identical IR; the schema (schema/ergostat.schema.json) and SPEC's block keys list runs-on. Files: ergostat/compute/compile.py, ergostat/spec/compile.py, ergostat/spec/ir.py, schema, tests/test_compute_compile.py, docs/SPEC.md. Full text: wave2-compute.md (the runs-on half of compute-pools-config). Budget: 90 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-worker-protocol
gaps.title: ergostat worker --stdio: the worker package, the protocol's frame, hello, beat and ping
gaps.definition: Problem: nothing on another machine can speak to the engine: there is no `ergostat worker` (ergostat/cli/__init__.py:356-369) and no protocol (compute-systems.md sections 2, 2.1, 3). The worker must run on a node with no ergostat installed, and ten later gaps add to it, so its shape is decided here: not one file but a small package of single-purpose modules, by the house rule (dev/knowledge/house-rules.md, Code). Change: ergostat/compute/worker/, standard library only, flat (its modules import each other by bare name, nothing from ergostat), with __main__.py so `python3 -I PATH/worker --stdio` runs it as a directory and a zipapp of the same folder runs the same way; `ergostat worker --stdio [--root DIR]` (new ergostat/cli/worker.py) calls the same main, and `ergostat worker --pack FILE` writes the zipapp for copying to a node. This gap makes frames.py (one JSON object a line each way, each with v (1), seq and type, at most 1 MiB; requests carry id) and serve.py (the loop and a table of message type to handler that each later gap extends with one module and one registration line). First line hello: node (a random 32-hex id kept in the root, never a host name, address or user), cpus, memory, disk.root, arch, os, backends, images, labels, slots (at most its CPUs, at most 64), runs. beat every 10 s; ping answered pong; another v answered error then exit; an unknown type answered error without ending. The root defaults to ~/.local/state/ergostat-worker/ and nothing is written elsewhere. A helper tests/compute_pipe.py starts the worker over a pipe. Done: the directory, the zipapp and the CLI entry each answer hello then pong under `python3 -I` (tested on the image's Python; if isolated mode cannot run a directory, __main__ loads its siblings by path and the test says so); a test asserts no module of the package imports outside the standard library and the package; the node id persists; seq rises by one per line; nothing written outside the root; SPEC gains a Compute systems section with one subsection per later gap to fill. Files: ergostat/compute/worker/{__main__,frames,serve}.py, ergostat/cli/worker.py, ergostat/cli/__init__.py, tests/compute_pipe.py, tests/test_compute_worker_protocol.py (eight tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 240 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-worker-keeper
gaps.title: The worker starts a run under a detached keeper, which runs it in its own process group and records its exit
gaps.definition: Problem: a run started by an SSH-launched worker would die with the session; the local wrapper only writes the exit (ergostat/spec/runrecord.py:22-30). This gap is the keeper's process control; its deadlines are compute-worker-keeper-deadlines. Change: new module ergostat/compute/worker/keeper.py and a `start` handler: `start` (run id checked against ^[0-9a-f]{32}$; refusals `bad name`, `full`, `limits over the node`) makes runs/RUN/ with run.json, in and a cwd, then starts a detached keeper (`--keep RUN`, setsid, SIGHUP ignored) and answers started or `refused no keeper`. The keeper forks the run in its own process group (pgid file written before exec, rlimits from the limits, on Linux PDEATHSIG and oom_score_adj), execs `/bin/sh -c COMMAND` with out/err to files, waits, and writes exit with the code and how (exit, or the signal). `kill {run}` writes a stop file; the keeper, seeing it within a quarter second, sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL after the grace and records how. It then waits for `done` or a day, removes its folder by name under the root, and exits. Done: a run reports its exit code; closing the worker's stdin leaves the run going and its exit is still written; on Linux a killed keeper takes its run with it (death signal); kill is TERM then KILL to the whole group; each refusal makes no folder and no process. At most 8 processes a test. Files: ergostat/compute/worker/keeper.py, ergostat/compute/worker/serve.py (one registration), tests/test_compute_keeper.py (five tests), docs/SPEC.md. Full text: wave2-compute.md (compute-worker-keeper, the process half). Budget: 180 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-worker-keeper-deadlines
gaps.title: The keeper holds a run's wall and lease deadlines on a clock that counts suspend
gaps.definition: Problem: a run on a node must not outlive its timeout or its lease when the session, or the engine, is gone; locally the timeout lives in the engine's follower (ergostat/spec/stream.py:36-38), which a node does not have. Change: new module ergostat/compute/worker/deadline.py used by the keeper. `start` writes the first deadline file (runs/RUN/deadline) from the spec's wall limit and lease. The keeper holds the wall deadline and the lease deadline, read from the file every quarter second, on a suspend-counting clock (CLOCK_BOOTTIME on Linux, the equivalent continuous clock on macOS; the module names the one it uses); an unreadable or garbage file keeps the last value and can never move a deadline later; at the earlier deadline it sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL after K and writes exit with how `wall` or `lease`. Done: a run past its wall is killed with how wall; a run whose lease deadline passes is killed with how lease; garbage written to the deadline file never extends; a deadline moved earlier takes effect within half a second; with the worker gone (stdin closed) both deadlines still hold; a simulated clock jump of an hour in the time of day changes nothing. At most 8 processes a test. Files: ergostat/compute/worker/deadline.py, ergostat/compute/worker/keeper.py, tests/test_compute_keeper_deadlines.py (six tests), docs/SPEC.md. Full text: wave2-compute.md (compute-worker-keeper, the deadline half). Budget: 130 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-worker-output
gaps.title: A node run's output sent by offset, resumed by attach, capped
gaps.definition: Problem: the engine records a run's lines as it follows a local file (ergostat/spec/stream.py:27-62); over a session that can be cut, lines must be addressable so a resend is recorded once (compute-systems.md section 2.3; order by offset, never time). Change: new module ergostat/compute/worker/output.py: a follower over each run's out and err sends `out {run, stream, offset, text}` (offset of the first byte; at most 64 KiB a line, split at a line end where possible; whole lines only until the run ends). `attach {run, out, err}` resends from those offsets; beat carries each run's offsets taken. Flow control: at most 4 MiB sent ahead of the engine's acknowledged offsets across runs. A file past limits.log (default 64 MiB, at most 1 GiB) stops its run with how `log over its cap`. `ended` comes after the run's last out; `done {run}` writes runs/RUN/done. Done: 10,000 lines covered exactly once in order; attach from a middle offset resends only from there; a line over 64 KiB rejoins exactly by offset; with the reader stalled at most 4 MiB is unacknowledged and RSS stays bounded (measured); a run over its log cap is stopped. Files: ergostat/compute/worker/output.py, ergostat/compute/worker/serve.py (registrations), tests/compute_pipe.py, tests/test_compute_output.py (six tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 220 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-worker-readings
gaps.title: Per-run CPU and memory on the node, in beats and at the end
gaps.definition: Problem: a local run's CPU and memory come from the shared sampler and the wait status (ergostat/costs/sampler.py:1-24; engine.py:1082-1089) and go on agent.ran/agent.failed as `resources`; a node run has neither (compute-systems.md section 2.8). Change: new module ergostat/compute/worker/sampler.py (standard library only, so a small tree sampler of its own): each process-backend run's tree (its process group and descendants by parent), from /proc on Linux and one `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=,pgid=,rss=,utime=,stime=` elsewhere, sampled once a second for ten seconds then every ten; per run CPU seconds, peak resident memory and peak process count. The latest is in each beat and the whole in `ended.resources` with the same keys a local run's resources carry (sampler.Sampler.finish, sampler.py:235). One sampling thread for all runs; readings are measurements, never events. Done: a 2 s CPU burn reports at least 1.5 CPU seconds; a 100 MB allocation reports a peak at least that; the keys equal a local run's; one thread samples four runs. Files: ergostat/compute/worker/sampler.py, ergostat/compute/worker/serve.py (one registration), tests/test_compute_readings.py (four tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 150 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-worker-restart-states
gaps.title: A starting worker lists its runs as running, gone or unknown, and sweeps by name
gaps.definition: Problem: a worker started again must say which runs it still holds and never call a run gone on a reading it did not make (compute-systems.md sections 2.4, 2.9); the local record decides alive by pid and start time only (ergostat/spec/runrecord.py:75-80). Change: new module ergostat/compute/worker/states.py: at start read every runs/RUN/ folder named ^[0-9a-f]{32}$; each run is `running` (pid alive with the recorded start time), `gone` only on an allowlisted reading (exit file written; or pid absent or restarted and its process group read as empty), else `unknown` (record unreadable, ps failed, group not read, run alive but keeper gone). hello.runs and beats carry the states. For unknown the worker at once stops the run by name (SIGTERM then SIGKILL to the recorded group) and keeps listing it unknown. A keeper gone with its run ended: the worker records the exit and cleans up. A sweep at start and hourly removes only run folders of that name form, resolved inside the root, when `done` exists or a day has passed since the end; never all-but-a-list. Done: the five cases in wave2-compute.md (running after restart; gone on exit file; ps failure is unknown and stopped; reused pid by group state; the sweep leaves other names, outward symlinks and young folders). Files: ergostat/compute/worker/states.py, ergostat/compute/worker/serve.py (hello and beat read it), tests/test_compute_restart_states.py (six tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 200 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-worker-lease-clock
gaps.title: The worker turns the engine's lease renewals into its keeper's deadline, on its own clock
gaps.definition: Problem: a keeper must kill a run whose lease the engine stopped renewing, by the engine's expiry, without comparing a time of the engine's with its own (compute-systems.md section 2.7); the keeper reads runs/RUN/deadline but only its first value is written. Change: new module ergostat/compute/worker/leaseclock.py: each engine message carrying `sent` (start's lease, `renew {run, fence, left, sent}`, ping) gives heard - sent on the worker's suspend-counting clock; `base` is the least over the last ten minutes. A run's lease deadline is sent + base + left of the latest renewal heard for its fence, written by temporary file and os.replace; an older fence is ignored; a later renewal of the same fence may move it either way. Only a renewal heard writes the file. K = grace(ttl)/4 (ergostat/leases/terms.py:38-41) is written beside it for the keeper's SIGKILL. Done: with random delays the deadline is never later than the engine's expiry plus the least delay seen; a clock of day an hour off changes nothing; a delayed renewal does not extend; an old fence is ignored; after a cut session the keeper kills by the last deadline plus K. Files: ergostat/compute/worker/leaseclock.py, ergostat/compute/worker/serve.py (one registration), tests/test_compute_lease_clock.py (five tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 120 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-node-connection
gaps.title: The engine's connection to each node of a pool: session, hello, beats, loss and reconnect
gaps.definition: Problem: the engine has no way to reach a worker (compute-systems.md sections 2.1, 3). This gap is the session; round trips and the status shown are compute-node-status. Change: ergostat/compute/connection.py, one Node per entry of each declared pool, named POOL/N by its place in the list and never by host, started with the engine and closed on close or swap: a subprocess (`ssh -T -o BatchMode=yes HOST ergostat worker --stdio`, or the pool's connect: argv) with pipes, one reader thread, stderr kept in the pool's log. It parses hello (version 1 only; labels must include the pool's), marks the node lost after three missed beats (30 s) or EOF, reconnects with backoff from 1 s doubling to ten minutes, and exposes request(msg) with ids and a timeout, and on(type, fn). Done: a connect: pool comes up; killing the worker loses the node at EOF, SIGSTOP after three beats; it returns with backoff; another v leaves the node out of service with the error kept; closing the engine ends every session and leaves no ssh or worker child; no host name, address or user appears in logs or events. Files: ergostat/compute/connection.py, ergostat/spec/engine.py, tests/test_compute_connection.py (six tests), docs/SPEC.md. Full text: wave2-compute.md (compute-node-connection, the session half). Budget: 200 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-node-status
gaps.title: Each node's round trips measured, and a pool's status in the heartbeat and /api/status
gaps.definition: Problem: the lease rule for node runs needs each node's least round trip, and nothing shows whether a pool's nodes are in service. Change in ergostat/compute/connection.py: a ping every 2 s per node, least_rtt(window=60) from the pongs; a per-pool status() (nodes in service, lost, slots, free, last error, least round trip) that goes in the heartbeat and in /api/status under `compute` (ergostat/web/server.py:447-455) only when the model has pools. No page changes: the status is data in an existing answer. Done: least_rtt is the least of the window and has no value before the first pong; a lost node's slots leave the pool's status at the next reading; a model without pools has no `compute` key; another v's error is in status; no host name, address or user appears in status. Files: ergostat/compute/connection.py, ergostat/web/server.py, tests/test_compute_connection.py (four tests), docs/SPEC.md. Full text: wave2-compute.md (compute-node-connection, the status half). Budget: 90 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-capacity-measures
gaps.title: A pool's slots as built-in measures, and the dispatcher's room capped by them
gaps.definition: Problem: a pool's capacity must read like any stock so a controller can hold a queue against it, and the dispatcher must stop sending to a pool whose slots are gone (compute-systems.md section 4). The workspace pools are the pattern (WORKSPACES, ergostat/spec/ir.py:205-212; numbers/measures.py:180, :190, :201; room at leases/dispatch.py:193-203). Change: COMPUTE = ^ergostat\.compute\.(slots|free|busy|nodes|lost)(?:@POOL)?$ and COMPUTE_MEASURES in ir.py, read from the connections' status in measures.py and recognised as built-in names. In tick_block a block with runs_on gets room = min(room, its pool's free slots less starts in flight), and globally at most 256 node runs held or draining before any start. A lost node's slots leave slots and free at once. No diagram changes: a model may declare a stock on these measures and it is drawn as any stock. Done: measures per pool and summed; a block with pool 8 and 2 free slots takes at most 2 items a pass; a lost node drops slots@POOL at the next reading; the 256 cap holds across two pools; a model without pools has no new measures and identical dispatch. Files: ergostat/spec/ir.py, ergostat/numbers/measures.py, ergostat/leases/dispatch.py, ergostat/compute/connection.py, tests/test_compute_capacity.py (five tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 160 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-remote-backend
gaps.title: A block with runs-on runs on a pool's node through the runner interface
gaps.definition: Problem: with the interface, the spec, the connection and the worker's output in place nothing joins them: runner(spec, block) returns local always and a runs-on block still runs here. Change: ergostat/compute/remote.py, a `remote` backend of the Runner protocol over a pool's connection. start(spec) picks a node in service with a free slot (fewest runs first), sends start with the RunSpec as JSON (the allowlisted environment, never the engine's) and returns a handle; `refused` raises Refused, which the engine turns into outcome["nack"] = {why, after: POOL_FULL_AFTER, count: False} as a full workspace pool does (ergostat/spec/engine.py:1170-1171). follow takes out lines in offset order, drops any below the offset taken, hands complete lines to take as stream.follow does, keeps the offset in the run's record after each batch, sends acks and returns at ended (how `wall` gives the timeout note). kill sends kill; alive is the node's last beat; resources is ended.resources; cleanup sends done. Done: a runs-on block over a same-machine worker records like the same block run locally; a forced resend records each line once; a refused start gives the item back uncounted; a lease kill reaches the node run; a block without runs-on is unchanged. Files: ergostat/compute/remote.py, ergostat/compute/runner.py, ergostat/spec/engine.py, tests/test_compute_remote_backend.py (five tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 260 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-lease-renew-on-node
gaps.title: A node run's lease renewed by the same activity as a local run's, killed on the node when not
gaps.definition: Problem: the watchdog renews a local run's lease by activity only at its look, after the expiry (ergostat/leases/dispatch.py:458, 470-476, activity at 506-525); a node's keeper kills at the expiry, so a node run kept alive only by activity the fold does not count would be killed first (compute-systems.md section 2.7). Change in remote.py and dispatch.py: for each node run the engine sends `renew {run, fence, left, sent}` at once after any move of the lease's expiry and every 2 s besides. On each tick while the lease has under half its TTL left it calls activity() as the watchdog does; later activity records the same `renewed` event (seen: activity), at most one a tick per run. Before start, the node's least round trip over the last minute (compute-node-status) must be at most grace(ttl)/4 (ergostat/leases/terms.py:38-41), else the item goes back uncounted as full; a running run whose node's round trips grow past it is killed. Fence and watchdog unchanged. Done: after a cut session the keeper kills by expiry plus grace/2, before the watchdog, the item goes back once and a later line is refused by the fence; a run active only through events about another item outlives its TTL as it does locally; a silent one is killed and expired, counted; a slow node is sent no start; renewals bounded. Files: ergostat/compute/remote.py, ergostat/leases/dispatch.py, ergostat/compute/connection.py, tests/test_compute_lease_on_node.py (six tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 230 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-reattach
gaps.title: A cut session to a node is resumed: held runs attached from their offsets, others killed
gaps.definition: Problem: when the session to a node ends and comes back within one engine process, the runs keep going but each follow has lost its stream, and a run the engine holds no lease for must never be left running (compute-systems.md section 2.4; the engine-restart half is compute-adopt-node-runs). Change in remote.py: on a node's hello after a reconnect, for each run listed: held by a lease of this engine (in dispatch.mine, fence matching) and running or gone, send `attach {run, out, err}` from the offsets in the run's record and the waiting follow resumes, recording each line once; not held, send kill then done once ended; unknown, keep the lease, record no end and send no renewal, so the watchdog expires it (ergostat/leases/dispatch.py:468-504) and the run ends agent.failed with the note `unknown on its node`. A followed run the hello does not list is ended `lost on its node` only when its lease has expired. Done: a session cut mid-run and reconnected records every line exactly once and ends agent.ran; an unheld run is killed and its folder removed; an unknown run keeps its lease until expiry with no renew sent; a missing run is not ended before its lease's expiry. Files: ergostat/compute/remote.py, ergostat/compute/connection.py, tests/test_compute_reattach.py (four tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 180 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-adopt-node-runs
gaps.title: An engine started again takes up the runs on nodes its record says it started
gaps.definition: Problem: after an engine restart no _ran thread waits for a run it had started, so nothing records its end; SPEC says taking up a run left by a stopped engine is not built (docs/SPEC.md:2379-2380). The parked rs-adopt-continued builds that for local runs; node runs need the same through the same mechanism (compute-systems.md section 2.4). Change: extend what rs-adopt-continued lands to node runs: a node run's record (pool, node index, run id, fence, offsets taken; written by compute-remote-backend) is read at engine start; once the node's hello lists the run the engine starts a follow thread through the remote backend's handle exactly as compute-reattach does, recording lines from the offset taken and the end, the lease kept and renewed. A run whose node never comes back keeps its lease until the watchdog expires it. The end is recorded before the run's record file is released. Done: an engine killed mid node run and restarted records the remaining lines once and ends agent.ran; a node gone at restart ends only at lease expiry, counted; local and node runs are adopted by one code path; SPEC's sentence is replaced. When rs-adopt-continued is resumed it should depend on compute-runner-interface. Files: ergostat/compute/remote.py, the adoption module, tests/test_compute_adopt.py (three tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 150 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-secrets
gaps.title: A pool's secrets read from files, sent at start, never written by ergostat
gaps.definition: Problem: a local run inherits the engine's whole environment (ergostat/spec/engine.py:995); a node run gets only the allowlisted one, so it has no way to receive a secret (compute-systems.md section 2.6). Change: the pool's `secrets: {NAME: file}` are read at each start by the remote backend (`~` expanded; an unreadable file refuses the start by name, item given back uncounted) and sent in start.secrets. On the worker a new module ergostat/compute/worker/secret.py keeps them in memory only: the process backend passes them to the keeper through an inherited pipe (never a file or argv) into the run's environment; docker later passes `-e NAME`. The worker replaces each secret's exact value in forwarded lines with `[secret NAME]` as a second layer. Records, events, run.json, beats and errors carry names only; agent.started gets `secrets: [names]`. Done: after a run the value is in no file under the worker's root, the engine's state folder, the event record or any log (a test walks and greps them all); the run sees it and agent.started names it; a printed secret is recorded masked; an unreadable file refuses the start uncounted. Files: ergostat/compute/remote.py, ergostat/compute/worker/secret.py, ergostat/compute/worker/keeper.py, tests/test_compute_secrets.py (four tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 140 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-work-in
gaps.title: A node run starts in a worktree at an exact commit sent as a git bundle
gaps.definition: Problem: a node run has an empty folder and cannot work on the model's repository (compute-systems.md section 2.5, In); locally workspace pools make worktrees (ergostat/workspaces/git.py:50-58). Change: RunSpec.work = {repo, commit} (a name in the pool's repos: and a commit id, never a branch), set when the block says `work: {repo, commit: FIELD}` naming an item field (one block key added to the compute compiler). On the worker a new module ergostat/compute/worker/work.py keeps one bare repository per name under its root (repos/NAME.git) and answers `need {repo, commit, have: [newest commits]}` when it lacks the commit; the engine makes a `git bundle create` of what is missing, sends it as `bundle` chunks of at most 1 MiB, 2 GiB in all, with size and SHA-256; the worker verifies, fetches and makes the run's folder a detached worktree at that commit. Bare repositories are pruned by age and a disk cap. Done: a run sees the tree at the commit (file content and git rev-parse HEAD); a later commit sends a smaller bundle; a wrong hash or over-cap bundle refuses the start uncounted; a branch name is refused; pruning removes only repositories under repos/ of the name form. Files: ergostat/compute/worker/work.py, ergostat/compute/{remote,spec,compile}.py, tests/test_compute_work_in.py (five tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 260 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-work-out
gaps.title: A node run's commits, artifacts and transcripts brought back, hashed, capped and fenced
gaps.definition: Problem: what a node run makes stays on the node and is removed with its folder (compute-systems.md section 2.5, Out); the factory's containers bring work out as a git bundle (dev/bin/agents.py:309-335), unreachable from a model. Change: RunSpec.out = {bundle, artifacts: [globs], transcripts: [globs]} from the block's `out:` key. When the run ends the worker (new module ergostat/compute/worker/results.py) bundles the commits on top of the given commit, collects files matching the globs inside the run folder only (symlinks resolving outside refused and said), and sends each as `result` chunks with size and SHA-256, capped (bundle 256 MiB, artifacts 1 GiB, transcripts 64 MiB by default). The engine verifies each, fetches the bundle into a side ref refs/ergostat/runs/RUN-FENCE of the named repository (never a branch) and keeps the rest under runs/RUN/ in the state folder; agent.ran carries names, sizes and hashes. A result after the lease ended is refused by the fence and said. `done` is sent only after the results are kept. Done: two commits arrive at the side ref and no branch moved; artifacts byte-exact, an outward symlink refused and named; over a cap refused and noted on the end; a late result refused and recorded. Files: ergostat/compute/worker/results.py, ergostat/compute/{remote,spec,compile}.py, tests/test_compute_work_out.py (five tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 260 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-docker-backend
gaps.title: The worker's Docker backend: a run in a named container under its limits
gaps.definition: Problem: the process backend cannot limit network or isolate files (compute-systems.md section 2.2, docker); the factory runs sessions in containers with hard limits (dev/bin/agents.py:53-54) only for itself. Change: new module ergostat/compute/worker/docker.py: backend `docker` when docker is on PATH (hello.backends, hello.images). The keeper runs `docker run -d --init --name ergostat-run-RUN --cpus --memory --memory-swap --pids-limit --network none(default) --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges -v RUNFOLDER:/work -w /work IMAGE /bin/sh -c COMMAND`, output redirected to the run folder's out/err by a wrapper in the container, records the container id in run.json, waits with docker wait and writes the exit; at its deadlines `docker stop -t K` then `docker rm -f`. Readings from the container's cgroup in the process backend's keys. `no such image` is refused at start. If compute-worker-restart-states has landed, it reads a container by its recorded id; otherwise that gap adds it. The sweep removes only containers named ergostat-run- plus 32 hex. SPEC says Docker is a resource limit, not a security boundary. Done: output, exit and readings arrive as a process run's; with network none a socket fails; after a cut session the keeper asked docker rm -f by expiry plus grace/2; tests skip without docker. Files: ergostat/compute/worker/docker.py, ergostat/compute/worker/keeper.py, tests/test_compute_docker.py (five tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 250 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-calls-from-node
gaps.title: A node run calls the engine back through a socket its worker forwards
gaps.definition: Problem: a local run calls `ergostat act`, `event --add`, `lease` and `item` through ERGOSTAT_SOCKET (ergostat/spec/engine.py:1005-1008, 1817-1819; ergostat/calls/); on a node there is no socket, so compute-runs-on-config refuses every runs-on block whose command uses calls. Change: new module ergostat/compute/worker/calls.py: the worker serves a Unix socket in each run's folder (runs/RUN/calls.sock, mounted for docker), puts its path in the run's ERGOSTAT_SOCKET and forwards each call as `call {run, id, body}`, at most 20 a second a run (beyond: `busy`). The engine answers as its own socket does (ergostat/calls/server.py's handler, the run's identity taken from the handle, never from the call) and the worker relays `answer`. ERGOSTAT_CMD on a node names the worker's `--call` mode, a client speaking the protocol of ergostat/calls/client.py. The compile refusal is lifted for program blocks. Done: a node run's `$ERGOSTAT_CMD event --add` is recorded caused by its run; a call naming another run's identity is answered as the caller's; the 21st call in a second is busy; a call after the lease ended is refused by the fence; check allows calling blocks. Files: ergostat/compute/worker/calls.py, ergostat/compute/{remote,compile}.py, ergostat/calls/server.py, tests/test_compute_calls.py (five tests), docs/SPEC.md. Budget: 250 net lines.

gaps.name: compute-demo
gaps.title: examples/compute-pair: items worked on two same-machine nodes, one lost mid-run
gaps.definition: Problem: nothing shows a compute pool working end to end and scripts/demo_check.py covers no compute model; examples/remote-pair/ with tests/test_remote_pair.py is the pattern. Change: examples/compute-pair/, a model with one item kind, a program block with `runs-on: pair`, and a pool of two nodes each `connect: [python3, -I, ../../ergostat/compute/worker, --stdio, --root, ...]` (the worker package run as a directory; roots under the demo's state folder), plus a stock and goal on ergostat.compute.free@pair so the capacity is drawn as any stock in Dynamics and as a plant input in Blocks (only what the model declares). run.sh starts it; a script kills one worker and its keepers mid-run; README says what to watch. Done: run.sh completes on macOS and Linux; tests/test_compute_pair.py::test_node_lost_item_reworked sees the node lost, slots@pair drop, the lease expire (counted), the item re-run on the other node and done, with no host names anywhere; demo_check passes with the demo; nothing undeclared is drawn. Files: examples/compute-pair/ (model, README.md, run.sh), tests/test_compute_pair.py, scripts/demo_check.py, docs/SPEC.md (one line). Budget: 150 net lines, model YAML counted.

gaps.name: regression-queue-test-counts
gaps.title: The merge queue records each suite's pytest counts, unknown when its log cannot say
gaps.definition: Problem: the queue keeps only rc, seconds and a SKIPPED count per suite (dev/bin/queue.py:111-114), so no measure can say main lost tests (regression-guarantees.md section 4). Change: a pure parser fac.counts(text) next to fac.outcomes (dev/bin/fac.py:582-588) reading pytest's final summary line from the suite's whole log, taking the last such line. In suites()'s one() each pytest suite (unit, browser, host) gains `counts: {passed, failed, skipped, deselected, errors}`; a suite with no summary line, stopped by a sibling, stalled or unreadable records `counts: "unknown"`, never zeros; a suite not run by rule (merge-pipeline-browser-only-on-its-paths) records `counts: "not_run"`, which is neither unknown nor zero. The landed run's queue_runs entry (queue.py:836-837) gains counts summed over the suites that ran, with `suites: [names]` saying which, or "unknown" if any that ran is. ruff and demo record none. Done: fac.counts parses every summary form pytest -q prints, xdist's included, and returns None without one; the existing skipped field and the browser skip rule (queue.py:111, 216-220) are unchanged; dev/README.md names the fields. Files: dev/bin/fac.py, dev/bin/queue.py, dev/README.md, tests/test_queue.py (four tests). Budget: 60 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-flake-writes-hold-state
gaps.title: A flake seen never takes a test out of main-broken, and a second break keeps the first clock
gaps.definition: Problem: the kind flake moves to seen on every flake.seen (ergostat.yaml:197-200) and four writers emit it without looking (dev/bin/onmain.py:74, queue.py:241-242, triage.py:76, manage.py:231), so a test still failing on main leaves main-broken; every flake.main-broken writes a fresh main_broken_at (onmain.py:92-94), restarting the repair clock; a flake fixed then seen again keeps its old times. Change: new dev/bin/flakes.py with one writer flakes.say(event, test, **data) that every flake writer calls. Under one lock file in the run dir it re-reads the item and writes synchronously with fac.add: flake.seen on a main-broken item writes flake.measured (counts times, no state move); flake.main-broken on a main-broken item updates main and unions gaps, leaving main_broken_at; either on a fixed item is a remake, a patch changeset setting times to 1 and removing main_fixed_at, fixed_by and green_passes; an unreadable item is written as today with the failure on stderr. Done: no other code emits flake.seen or flake.main-broken (grep test over dev/bin, which later writers such as merge-pipeline-browser-daily-on-main must also pass); the three state rules hold; two concurrent writers never lose a state; `ergostat check` has no errors. Files: dev/bin/flakes.py, dev/bin/{onmain,queue,triage,manage}.py, ergostat.yaml, tests/test_factory.py (five tests). Budget: 120 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-flake-main-fixed
gaps.title: A test broken on main leaves main-broken when it passes twice alone on a newer main
gaps.definition: Problem: nothing takes an item out of main-broken (ergostat.yaml:197-200; the only writer is dev/bin/onmain.py:94 and nothing emits fixed), so a stock of tests failing on main would only rise. Change: declare `flake.main-fixed: fixed`. New dev/bin/mend.py as a block main-mend in dev/model/landing.yaml (every 30m, pool 1, a lease, timeout 30m): fetch the pushed main, wait for a quiet machine (fac.wait_quiet), take at most `[gates] mend_most` main-broken items oldest first (default 5, ceiling 20), and run their tests alone twice on that sha in a suite container with -rA (a browser test with the browser suite's command and playwright), results from fac.outcomes over the whole log. A test passing both gets flake.main-fixed with passed_on, main_fixed_at and fixed_by: main-mend, written as a patch changeset whose first op tests the item's `main` as read, and only if that main is passed_on or an ancestor of it, so a newer break written in between refuses it. Failed, skipped, not collected, quarantined or unreadable is unknown and stays main-broken. Done: only two passes on the pushed main clear an item; a refused patch also refuses the state move; at most mend_most a run; dev/README.md describes the block. Files: dev/bin/mend.py, dev/model/landing.yaml, ergostat.yaml, dev/factory.toml, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py (five tests). Budget: 150 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-flake-fixed-after-green
gaps.title: A seen flake is fixed after N green queue runs that each say it passed
gaps.definition: Problem: flake.fixed is declared (ergostat.yaml:200) and emitted nowhere, so no flake leaves seen; the queue's green runs could clear them, but its unit and browser commands print no PASSED lines (dev/factory.toml:158, :170), so a deleted or renamed flake would count as passed. Change: add `p` to the -r flags of `[suites] unit` and `browser` (on top of the -rfEs that merge-pipeline-browser-names-its-failures gives browser, the same line), checking fac.failed_tests and queue.nowhere (queue.py:198-213) still read the same lines. After a green landing (next to gap.merged, queue.py:842) flakes.green(logs) takes each seen item not quarantined, at most 50, and reads its outcome from the run's unit and browser logs with fac.outcomes: a pass raises green_passes by one (a patch testing the value read), unknown changes nothing (a suite not run in that batch is unknown for its tests), and at `[gates] flake_fixed_after` (default 5, ceiling 50) it writes flake.fixed with fixed_by: green-runs and fixed_on. Every flake.seen through flakes.say sets green_passes to 0, so the count is consecutive, in queue order. A failure here never fails or delays a landing. Done: N consecutive green runs naming the test PASSED fix it; a seen between restarts the count; a test absent from the log never counts; README says how a flake leaves seen. Files: dev/factory.toml, dev/bin/flakes.py, dev/bin/queue.py, dev/README.md, tests/test_queue.py, tests/test_factory.py. Budget: 110 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-flake-fixed-by-hand
gaps.title: A person can say a flake is fixed, and the quarantine's release is one event
gaps.definition: Problem: a test that was deleted or renamed stays seen or main-broken forever, and so does every goal on those stocks; manage.py has a `flake` command that writes flake.seen (dev/bin/manage.py:228-233) and no way out. The quarantine's release is a bare flake.measured with quarantined: false (dev/bin/fac.py:594-598, on main today), so the record cannot tell a release from any measurement. Change: `manage.py flake-fixed TEST --why W` writes flake.fixed from seen or main-broken with fixed_by (the person) and why, and records an intervention with intervene("flake-fixed", ...) (manage.py:56); an item in neither state is refused with a message. fac.beside's release writes flake.released (quarantined: false, released_at), declared as a no-state event in the kind's comment; quarantined folds as before. Done: the command moves an item from either state to fixed and records one intervention; it refuses an unknown test or one already fixed; a release is one flake.released event after which quarantined is false; dev/README.md 'Record an intervention' lists the command. Files: dev/bin/manage.py, dev/bin/fac.py, ergostat.yaml, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py (three tests). Budget: 50 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-flake-rate-counts-excused
gaps.title: flake-rate counts the queue's excused flakes, and has no value with no runs
gaps.definition: Problem: flake-rate reads only the gaps' retries over their queue_attempts (dev/bin/measure.py:174-176), and only triage writes retries (triage.py:77). A red run the queue itself excuses as a flake (dev/bin/queue.py:235-244) writes flake.seen and lands with `excused` in its suites_queue but counts nowhere, so the goal flakes-rare (dev/model/measures.yaml:115-119) undercounts; with no runs it reads 0.0, which fails open. Change: flake-rate = (triage retries in the window + queue runs in the window whose landed gaps carry suites_queue.excused, each run once by batch_id) / the queue runs in the window (distinct `run` in queue_runs, as merges-per-hour counts them, measure.py:160-164). A window with no queue runs exits 1 with no value. The docstring lists flake-rate among the measures with no value, and the auxiliary's description says it counts both. Done: an excused run raises the rate; a run excused for a batch of three counts once; no runs gives no value, never 0.0; triage retries count as before. Files: dev/bin/measure.py, dev/model/measures.yaml, tests/test_factory_measure_runs.py (three tests). Budget: 30 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-escapes-from-reverts
gaps.title: A revert on main is recorded as an escape of the gap it reverts, and escapes-found gets a sensor
gaps.definition: Problem: the stock escapes counts reverted merges, but gap.reverted is entered only by hand (ergostat.yaml:153-154) and its inflow escapes-found has no sensor (dev/model/pools.yaml:66-69), so a revert commit on main is invisible. Change: in `upgrade.py watch` (block main-watch, dev/model/landing.yaml:358-364; dev/bin/upgrade.py:24-41) a step escapes.watch() in new dev/bin/escapes.py walks `git rev-list --first-parent` from the last commit read (run/escapes.json) to the pushed main, at most 200 commits (said when hit), looking for `This reverts commit <sha>`. A reverted commit is matched to a merged gap first by its second parent being the gap's reviewed_head, then by main_sha (main_sha is the batch's pushed head, shared by a batch's gaps and, after merge-pipeline-gaps-md-regenerated-on-land, a commit that is no gap's merge, so it identifies a gap only when exactly one gap carries it). A match writes gap.reverted with reverted: true, revert_sha, reverted_at. No match writes intervention.recorded as intervention/reverted-<sha12>, class reverted-unmatched, which dev/bin/risk.py counts as an escape as it does an unmatched main-broken (risk.py:79-88). Ids make a second read a no-op. escapes-found gets a sensor `pools.py read escapes-day`. Done: a revert is recorded once however often main-watch runs; a revert of one merge of a batch of three blames only that gap; an unmatched one still counts; check reports no flow without a sensor in pools.yaml; a git error stops only this step; README says reverts are found by main-watch. Files: dev/bin/{escapes,upgrade,risk,pools}.py, dev/model/pools.yaml, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py (five tests). Budget: 130 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-guarantees-model
gaps.title: The guarantees system: main's failing tests as a stock, held at zero by main-green
gaps.definition: Problem: when main breaks the model shows it only as one main-broken intervention (dev/model/interventions.yaml:9-12); no stock counts the tests failing on main and no goal says main is green (regression-guarantees.md sections 3, 6a). Change: ergostat.yaml gains a system `guarantees` within oversight, showing stock.main-failing-tests. New dev/model/guarantees.yaml: stock main-failing-tests ({items: flake, state: main-broken, every: 1m}); flows main-tests-broken (entering main-broken over 1d) and main-tests-fixed (entering fixed where fixed_by: main-mend, equation stock over a parameter main-repair-time); goal main-green (hold <= 0, tolerance 0, critical, on-stale off, per item); a named balancing loop main-repair. Wiring: remedy-when (interventions.yaml:43-50) gains `main: goal.main-green.off`, remedy's out gains flow.main-tests-fixed, and main-mend gets out flow.main-tests-fixed, so the loop closes through people and an existing program. Asked of the owner in the record and not built: should main-green off also hold the queue for batches that do not touch the failing tests. Done: check reports no errors and no missing feedback for main-green; main-repair drawn balancing; a break turns the goal off and its main-fixed turns it holding; stale counts as off; README gains 'Regression guarantees'. Files: ergostat.yaml, dev/model/{guarantees,interventions,landing}.yaml, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py (three tests). Budget: 40 net lines of code.

gaps.name: regression-tests-passing-goal
gaps.title: tests-passing on main as a measure, with a goal that it does not fall over ten merges
gaps.definition: Problem: nothing measures how many tests main passes, so a gap that skips tests, or makes them fail to collect, passes every gate unseen (regression-guarantees.md section 4). This is not the filed cx-test-ratio's count: that one counts the tests defined in the code (in the code-health cache, for the ratio of tests to code); this one counts the tests a queue run on main actually passed, which falls when a test is skipped, deselected or broken though still defined. The record says so, and the two are never summed. Change: new dev/bin/passing.py with two readings. `tests-passing` is the summed `passed` of the latest landed queue run on main whose counts cover unit, browser and host (runs where browser was not run by rule are passed over, never read as a fall), chosen by main's first-parent seq, never by time. `tests-passing-change` is the latest less the earliest such run within the last 10 seqs, each sha once, computed by the trend-by-seq helper the filed cx-trend-auxiliaries uses for the code-health stocks (measure.py:357-420), reused and if need be given a values argument, never copied. `counts: unknown` on the latest full run, fewer than two full runs in the window or no checkout gives no value (exit 1); a missing summary never counts as zero. dev/model/guarantees-passing.yaml: auxiliaries tests-passing and tests-passing-change (every 30m) and a goal tests-not-falling (>= 0, tolerance 0, on-stale off), left unserved until regression-guarantees-wired. Done: both readings come from the recorded counts by seq through the shared helper; unknown gives no value; a browser-skipped run between two full runs changes nothing; a fixture with two runs and fewer passed turns the goal off; check has no errors and the only new finding is missing-feedback@tests-not-falling; README lists the measure and how it differs from the test ratio. Files: dev/bin/passing.py, dev/bin/measure.py (the helper's argument, if needed), dev/model/guarantees-passing.yaml, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory_measure_runs.py (five tests). Budget: 70 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-escape-rate-goal
gaps.title: escape-rate, escapes per merged gap, held under the owner's setpoint
gaps.definition: Problem: the stock escapes (dev/model/pools.yaml:28-32) is cumulative and has no goal; it only feeds the pools' risk (pools.yaml:39-43), so nothing says quality is slipping (regression-guarantees.md sections 3, 4). Change: `pools.py read escape-rate`: escapes over merged gaps in the last 14 days, from risk.evidence (dev/bin/risk.py:62-102) restricted to that window by merge time, reusing the evidence with no second count; no merged gaps in the window gives no value (exit 1). dev/model/guarantees-escapes.yaml: auxiliary escape-rate (driven-by +stock.escapes), parameter escape-tolerance (0.05, a placeholder the owner sets, like risk-tolerance at pools.yaml:87-90), goal escapes-rare (<= escape-tolerance, on-stale off), left unserved until regression-guarantees-wired. The pool tuner is unchanged. Done: the reading equals escapes over merged gaps of the window on a fixture; no merges gives no value; the setpoint is a parameter; the existing risk tests pass as they are; check has no errors. Files: dev/bin/pools.py, dev/bin/risk.py (a window argument if needed), dev/model/guarantees-escapes.yaml, tests/test_factory.py (three tests). Budget: 40 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-flake-measures
gaps.title: Flakes open, the hours main stays broken and the hours a flake stays unfixed, with goals
gaps.definition: Problem: nothing measures how long main stays broken or a flake stays unfixed, and no goal names the oldest flake (regression-guarantees.md sections 3, 4). Change: dev/bin/flakes.py gains readings taken from the items' moves in record order (`ergostat item ID --json`, as dev/bin/times.py and watch.py:92-101 read them), never by comparing stamps, over at most 500 items (said when hit). main-repair-hours: the median over 14 days, per stay, from the move into main-broken from another state to the move to fixed; a repeat break inside one stay does not restart the clock. flake-fix-hours: the median from the move into seen to fixed. With no ended stay in the window either gives no value. dev/model/guarantees-flakes.yaml: stock flakes-open ({items: flake, state: seen}); goal flakes-few (<= 3, per item so the oldest is named, on-stale off); auxiliaries main-repair-hours and flake-fix-hours; goal main-repaired-fast (<= 24, on-stale off); flows flakes-seen and flakes-fixed with item sensors. Setpoints are parameters; the goals stay unserved until regression-guarantees-wired. Done: repair hours run from the first break of a stay; a remake starts a new stay; check has no errors. Files: dev/bin/flakes.py, dev/model/guarantees-flakes.yaml, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py (four tests). Budget: 90 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-quarantine-goals
gaps.title: The quarantine as a stock that must not grow, and the age of its oldest test as a measure
gaps.definition: Problem: the quarantine is a file only a reviewer reads, 'added and released by hand' (tests/quarantine.txt:1-3); it holds eight tests today, the oldest from 2026-11-21, and nothing says it is growing or stale (regression-guarantees.md sections 3, 4). It needs only what is on main: the list with its `when` column and fac.quarantine (dev/bin/fac.py:566-571), both from the merged quarantine-list-honest; it does not wait for flake-quarantine-continued. A goal that is off from its first reading would hold the coordinator's commander on for good, so the setpoint comes from the evidence. Change: new dev/bin/held.py reads the list on the pushed main and cross-checks it with the flake items marked quarantined. `held.py quarantined` gives the number listed; `held.py quarantine-oldest-days` the age of the oldest `when`. A list or date that cannot be read gives no value; a listed test with no quarantined flake item, or the reverse, is named on stderr. dev/model/guarantees-quarantine.yaml: stock quarantined; parameter quarantine-most, set to the count on main the day this is built (8 at filing; the implementor reads it and says the number in the record; the owner lowers it as tests are released); goal quarantine-small (<= quarantine-most, on-stale off), which holds on its first reading and goes off only when the quarantine grows, unserved until regression-guarantees-wired; auxiliary quarantine-oldest-days with no goal yet. Asked of the owner in the record in one sentence and not built: how many days a test may stay quarantined; a goal on the age is added only with that answer and only once the oldest test is under it. Done: count and oldest age match the list on a fixture; unreadable gives no value; mismatches are named; quarantine-small holds on main as it is and is off with one test added; check has no errors and no goal on the age. Files: dev/bin/held.py, dev/model/guarantees-quarantine.yaml, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py (four tests). Budget: 60 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-gate-catches
gaps.title: How often each gate catches something, as evidence for keeping or changing it
gaps.definition: Problem: a gate that fails is a finding, not a measure; nothing counts how often each gate catches something, so nobody can see a gate that never does (regression-guarantees.md sections 3, 4, 6c).
