Change: dev/bin/times.py already reads each gap's events incrementally (times.py:3-5, :132-160); its per-gap output (gap.timed) gains `catches: {gate: n}`, counted from the gap's gap.sent-back events by sent_back_by (queue, triage, review, lint, measure-runs) and from the implementor's refusals for strays. Gates are in an allowlist CATCHING; an unlisted sender is counted under `unlisted` and named on stderr. `measure.py gate-catches-GATE` gives the catches in the last 14 days by the event's time. dev/model/guarantees-gates.yaml: one auxiliary per listed gate and no goal, since a quiet gate is evidence, not a regression. The simplifier's brief (dev/prompts/simplify.md) names each gate with no catch in 30 days as a candidate to question, never to remove unasked. Done: catches per gate equal a fixture's sent-back events; an unlisted sender is counted and named; the brief carries the quiet gates; check has no errors. Files: dev/bin/times.py, dev/bin/measure.py, dev/model/guarantees-gates.yaml, dev/prompts/simplify.md, tests/test_factory_times.py (three tests). Budget: 90 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-lessons-recurring
gaps.title: A lesson's class found again after a brief carried it is counted, and held low
gaps.definition: Problem: first-pass-with-lessons compares yields (dev/model/knowledge.yaml:74-79), but nothing counts a review finding of a class the gap's own brief carried, which is the lesson failing as a guarantee (regression-guarantees.md sections 3, 4). The data exists: the librarian records each review's classes (review.measured: classes, dev/bin/librarian.py:1-11) and each brief records the lesson ids it carried (knowledge, dev/bin/knowledge.py:264-272). Change: `measure.py lessons-recurring` (in knowledge_reading, dev/bin/measure.py:291-311): over reviews written in the last 14 days, the count of classes found that are in the reviewed gap's first brief's carried lesson ids. A review with no recorded classes is left out and counted on stderr; no reviews in the window gives no value. dev/model/guarantees-lessons.yaml: auxiliary lessons-recurring and goal lessons-hold (<= 2, on-stale off, the setpoint a parameter), unserved until regression-guarantees-wired, where its loop goes to the librarian. Done: a finding of a carried class counts and one of a class not carried does not; check has no errors. Files: dev/bin/measure.py, dev/model/guarantees-lessons.yaml, tests/test_factory_knowledge.py (three tests). Budget: 40 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-escape-learning
gaps.title: Each escape becomes an item, and the librarian is asked once for its lesson or test
gaps.definition: Problem: an escape (a reverted merge, main broken after a merge, a gap named as a cause) only lowers the pools (dev/model/pools.yaml:113-121); no lesson is asked for and no test is added (regression-guarantees.md section 4). Change: a kind `escape` (escape/<gap>; states found, learned, dismissed) in ergostat.yaml. `librarian.py escapes` (every 30m) reads the escaped gaps from risk.evidence (dev/bin/risk.py:62-102, refactored to also return the blamed ids) and writes escape.found with the cause and evidence for each one without an item, at most 10 a run. A block escape-librarian takes escape at found under a lease (pool 1, attempts 2), so each escape gets one step: one small AI call with the librarian prompt and the gap's definition, diff stat and cause, which either proposes a lesson through the existing gated knowledge-change (dev/bin/librarian.py:30-32) or requests a gap adding the missing test (gap.requested, source escape), then writes escape.learned; a step that cannot decide writes escape.dismissed with why. guarantees-escapes.yaml gains the stock escapes-unlearned and the loop escape-learning. Done: one item per escape however often the scan runs; one step per item; the outcome is a gated proposal or a requested gap, never a direct edit; within the day's AI cap (fac.may_spend); check has no errors. Files: ergostat.yaml, dev/bin/librarian.py, dev/bin/risk.py, dev/model/{guarantees-escapes,knowledge}.yaml, dev/prompts/librarian.md, tests/test_factory_knowledge.py (four tests). Budget: 150 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-guarantees-wired
gaps.title: Every regression goal reaches the coordinator through one block, and every loop is named
gaps.definition: Problem: the measure gaps land their goals unserved, each missing feedback (docs/SPEC.md:2232), on purpose so parallel gaps never edit the same lines; until something serves them a broken guarantee shows only as a check finding (regression-guarantees.md section 6a). Change in dev/model/guarantees.yaml: an expr block guarantees-off, the max of tests-not-falling, escapes-rare, flakes-few, main-repaired-fast, quarantine-small and lessons-hold, each .off, feeding factory-off as one new input (dev/model/measures.yaml:132-147), so the coordinator keeps one commander, as code-health-off does (dev/model/code-health.yaml:163-172). A goal goes into guarantees-off only if it holds on main the day this is built: the gap reads each goal's state on a copy of the live record, says them in its record, and any that is off then (with its reason) is left out of the expression with a comment and listed for the owner, so the commander is never on from its first tick for a known standing cause. There is no goal on the quarantine's age (regression-quarantine-goals). escapes-rare and lessons-hold also reach the librarian's escape step. `loops:` names flake-repair, quarantine-release, escape-learning and tests-kept. The guarantees system's show: lists main-failing-tests, flakes-open, quarantined and escape-rate. dev/README.md gets one table of measure, goal and the loop that acts. Done: check has no errors, no missing-feedback for any goal in dev/model/guarantees*.yaml that is in the expression, and every named loop balancing; each goal's loop closes through a block (spec.loop(n).closes, the pattern of tests/test_factory.py:3774-3787); turning any one included goal off sets factory-off; on the live record's copy factory-off is not commanded by guarantees-off at the first reading. Files: dev/model/{guarantees,measures,knowledge}.yaml, ergostat.yaml, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py (four tests). Budget: 20 net lines of code.

gaps.name: regression-guarantees-on-diagrams
gaps.title: A broken guarantee is seen off in Dynamics, Blocks and Process, and a browser test fails if it is drawn holding
gaps.definition: Problem: the proposal claims each broken guarantee shows through what already exists, with no new page or panel (regression-guarantees.md section 5): an excess beside its stock in Dynamics, red periods on its block's chart in Blocks (ergostat/web/static/charts.js:545), a state items enter and never leave in Process, and the off goals on the guarantees box. No test checks those claims. Change: no UI code is expected. The test goes in tests/test_diagram_rendering.py, one of the four files the queue's browser command already names (dev/factory.toml:170), so it runs in the queue with no change to the command; no new browser test file is made. It reads a fixture copy of the factory model (ergostat.yaml and dev/model/, which the browser suite's skip rule never skips) with a record that breaks main and leaves a flake in seen, and checks: Dynamics draws main-failing-tests with its desired value and an excess above zero; in Blocks main-green's comparator is off and its chart marks the off period; Process shows the flake kind's seen state with items in and none out; the guarantees box lists its off goals first. Screenshots go to docs/screenshots/. The test is broken once on purpose with the goal forced holding to see it fail, and that run is said in the record. A claim that does not hold is fixed in the model's layout or narrowed in the proposal's section 5, never by a new panel. Done: the four checks pass in the browser suite as the queue runs it; the forced-holding run fails; screenshots committed. Files: tests/test_diagram_rendering.py, docs/screenshots/, docs/proposals/regression-guarantees.md if narrowed. Budget: 30 net lines outside tests, none expected.

gaps.name: regression-fixes-hold-goal
gaps.title: The repair template's goal that no fix regressed in the last 14 days, and the stock in SPEC's parts table
gaps.definition: Problem: the repair template has the stock regressed-fixes and the flows fixes-regressed and fixes-reverted (ergostat/library/templates/repair/template.yaml:49, :63-64) but its only goals are no-open-failures and fixes-answered (:66-67), so a fix that regressed breaks no goal. A goal on the stock itself could never recover, since a denied revert-fix leaves the failure regressed for good (docs/SPEC.md:6710), and SPEC's parts table leaves the stock out (docs/SPEC.md:6723). Change: template.yaml gains an auxiliary fixes-regressed-recent (sensor {items: ergostat.failure, entering: regressed, over: 14d}, driven-by +flow.fixes-regressed) and a goal fixes-hold (<= 0, tolerance 0, on-stale off), which recovers when a window passes with no new regression and is served by the existing gated revert ask; if check finds no block serving it, the template's person approver block reads it. SPEC section 12r's parts table lists regressed-fixes, fixes-regressed-recent and fixes-hold and says why the goal is on the window. Done: a regressed fix turns fixes-hold off and it holds again after a window with none; a denied revert does not hold it off for good; check on a model using the template reports no errors or missing feedback. Files: ergostat/library/templates/repair/template.yaml, docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_repair_verify.py (three tests). Budget: 25 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-template
gaps.title: A library template, regressions, that gives a user's model passing counts, escapes and regressed fixes
gaps.definition: Problem: ergostat adds nothing of its own accord, so a user gets regression guarantees only by asking, and there is no template to ask for (regression-guarantees.md section 6b). Change: ergostat/library/templates/regressions/template.yaml, used as `uses: {regressions: {use: regressions, with: {...}}}`, each part opt-in through with:. Passing counts: an auxiliary tests-failing whose sensor runs the model's declared `claims: tests` command (docs/SPEC.md:5236) on a schedule through a small reader `python -m ergostat.regressions counts` with a pytest-style summary parser in new ergostat/regressions.py; a run that cannot be read or has no summary gives no value; goal tests-green (<= 0, on-stale off). Escapes: an auxiliary on builtin ergostat.trust.contradicted@${block} (SPEC:5299-5309), goal claims-kept (<= ${escape-share}). Regressed model changes: builtin ergostat.model.regressed (SPEC:5187), goal changes-hold (<= 0). Regressed fixes: when the model also uses repair, a parameter names its instance and the template reads fixes-hold without duplicating it. Every goal is served by a person block by default, the agent a parameter. Flakes and quarantine are left out. Done: a model using it checks clean with no missing feedback; a failing run turns tests-green off; an unreadable command leaves it stale and off. Files: the template, ergostat/regressions.py, tests/test_regressions_template.py (four tests). Budget: 150 net lines.

gaps.name: regression-template-docs-demo
gaps.title: SPEC and the agent guide describe regression guarantees, and a demo uses the template
gaps.definition: Problem: once the regressions template exists nothing tells a user or an agent when to offer it, and no demo shows it working (regression-guarantees.md milestone gap 7). Change: docs/SPEC.md gains a short section next to 12g (claims and trust) and 12r (repair) covering the four parts of a guarantee (a measured quantity, a setpoint, a loop that acts, seen broken on the diagrams), the template's parts, and what holding does not promise (proposal section 6c). docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md gets one paragraph: offer the template when a model declares `claims: tests` or uses repair, and never add it unasked. examples/image-squeeze, which declares claims: (examples/image-squeeze/lab.yaml:43), uses the template. Done: the SPEC section and the guide paragraph exist and match the template's parts; image-squeeze uses the template, passes `scripts/demo_check.py image-squeeze` and `ergostat check` with no errors, and its goals hold in the healthy demo. Files: docs/SPEC.md, docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md, examples/image-squeeze/lab.yaml, and the demo's own check if one names its goals. Budget: 20 net lines outside docs/ and examples/.

gaps.name: regression-test-build-hours-park
gaps.title: A test that a gap past its build hours is parked
gaps.definition: Problem: the kill rule parks a gap whose building took more than `[gates] build_hours` (dev/bin/implement.py:190-193; dev/factory.toml:17), but no test parks a gap on build_hours; the proposal lists that part of F8 as untested (regression-guarantees.md section 2a), so a refactor that drops the check would land green. Change: one test in tests/test_factory.py on the Factory fixture (GATES, tests/test_factory.py:117). A gap with build_hours at the limit, taken by the implementor, is parked with the kill rule's reason and starts no session; one just under the limit is built (tests/test_factory.py:1263 already folds one just under). The test is broken once on purpose, with the comparison flipped, to see it fail, and that run is said in the gap's record. Done: the test parks at the limit and builds below it; it fails with the check removed. Files: tests/test_factory.py. Acceptance test: test_a_gap_past_its_build_hours_is_parked. Budget: 0 net lines outside tests/.

gaps.name: regression-test-empty-install-idle
gaps.title: A test that an empty install runs nothing
gaps.definition: Problem: invariant 12 says an empty install runs nothing (CLAUDE.md:52-53), and the proposal notes that no test checks it (regression-guarantees.md section 2b, U5 row), so a default block, sensor or template added by accident would land green. Change: one test that starts the engine on an empty model (a folder with a minimal ergostat.yaml and no parts), steps it for a few ticks, and asserts that no block runs (no agent.started), no sensor reads, no item is made, and the record holds only ergostat's own start events. The test is broken once on purpose, with a stray default part added, to see it fail, and that run is said in the gap's record. Done: the test passes on main; it fails when a default part is added. Files: tests/test_empty_install.py (new). Acceptance test: test_an_empty_install_runs_nothing. Budget: 0 net lines outside tests/.

gaps.name: conformance-list-files
gaps.title: Conformance lists: a list file read and validated, every limit refused by name
gaps.definition: Problem: the owner wants the features we wish we had listed, each tested, and the passing count kept as a stock. docs/proposals/conformance-stock.md section 1 defines the list file (`list`, `description`, `cases` each with check, timeout, asked, from, description) and nothing on main reads one. Change: a small pure module ergostat/library/run/conformance_lists.py. read(folder, names) -> Lists reads <folder>/<name>.yaml in order and raises ListError(name, why) on the first problem, never returning a partial result; Case(list, name, id = case/<list>/<name>, check, timeout_s, asked, from_, description); Lists.cases, Lists.declared and Lists.digest (sha256 over the named files' bytes in name order). Refused by list name and key: a missing file; YAML that is not a mapping; list: not equal to the file name; a name repeated in names; a name off ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$; a case without check; a timeout unparseable or over 10m (default 1m); asked not a bool (default true); an unknown key; over 500 cases in a list, over 20 lists, over 500 cases across them. Durations use ergostat.durations.parse_duration. Done: the digest moves only with the named files; the module imports nothing from ergostat.spec beyond durations. Files: the module, tests/test_conformance_lists.py (eleven tests). Budget: 140 net lines.

gaps.name: conformance-runner-runs-cases
gaps.title: Conformance runner: runs each case in its own process group and reports met, unmet or broken
gaps.definition: Problem: the proposal's runner (conformance-stock.md section 2) does not exist; `conformance` is not in the library's program table (ergostat/library/run/__main__.py:9-12). A run sensor's timeout kills only the process it started (ergostat/spec/engine.py:2402-2406) and a non-zero exit records nothing (:2407-2410). Change: ergostat/library/run/conformance.py, registered as `conformance --folder F --lists NAME... [--when CMD] [--budget SECONDS] [--instance NAME]`. It reads the lists (a ListError prints the reason and exits 2, running nothing); works out a key from --when's stdout and the lists' digest, and with the last run's key (common.kept) prints only the declared count; otherwise increments a run counter and runs each case one at a time with shell=True and start_new_session, killing the whole process group at the timeout (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 2 s): exit 0 met, 1 unmet, anything else, a timeout or a command that cannot start broken. It stops starting cases when the budget left is under the next timeout, naming each skipped case on stderr. Per case run it prints one observation line {event: case.met|case.unmet|case.broken, item: case/<list>/<name>, data: {list, asked, description, from, run, key, said}}; the declared count is the last line and the exit is 0 whatever the cases said. Done: a hung check's children are killed; run numbers rise by one and never repeat; the lines pass engine.observations. Files: the program, __main__.py, __init__.py, tests/test_conformance_runner.py (ten tests). Budget: 200 net lines.

gaps.name: conformance-runner-withdraws
gaps.title: Conformance runner: a case taken off its list, or a list dropped, is withdrawn
gaps.definition: Problem: without this a case taken off a list stays met and keeps counting (conformance-stock.md section 2 step 5); the runner prints only the cases it ran. A sensor's command can read the record back through $ERGOSTAT_CMD (ergostat/spec/engine.py:2359-2367) with `item --kind case --json` (docs/SPEC.md:1729). Change in ergostat/library/run/conformance.py, after the cases run and only on a real run: read the items of kind case and print {event: case.withdrawn, item: id, data: {list, run}} for each item not already withdrawn whose id is case/<list>/<name> where either <list> was read and <name> is not in it, or <list> is not among --lists. Judge by the id's prefix, never by data.list. If the item read fails (no $ERGOSTAT_CMD, a non-zero exit, output that is not JSON) withdraw nothing, say so on stderr, and still exit 0 with the count. An id not of that form is left alone and named on stderr. Done: a removed case is withdrawn once and not again on a second run; with two lists a removal touches only its list; a dropped list has every item withdrawn; an unreadable list stops the run before any withdrawal; a failed item read changes nothing. Files: the program, tests/test_conformance_runner.py (five tests). Budget: 60 net lines.

gaps.name: conformance-template
gaps.title: use: conformance, a built-in template: the case kind, the met count as a stock, its flows and goals
gaps.definition: Problem: any project should be able to count its wishes without writing its own bench.py; the only model that does is hand-written (examples/image-squeeze/benchmark.yaml:9-25, :57-72, :114-117). Change: ergostat/library/templates/conformance.yaml, `once: true`, with the proposal's section 2 body: the item kind case (states unmet, met, broken, withdrawn; show list, description, from, asked, run, key, said); stocks conformance-declared (the runner's number), conformance-met and conformance-wanted (items: sensors); auxiliary conformance-unaccounted; flows conformance-gained and conformance-lost; goals every-wish (<= 0), nothing-lost (<= 0) and every-case-run (== 0). Parameters: folder and lists (required), when (optional, passed as --when), every (default 10m), timeout (default 30m, the sensor's timeout and passed as --budget ${timeout:seconds}). It has reading:, example: and a stand-in list folder inside the template (two cases, true and false) so it runs offline. SPEC §2a and docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md say how to use it, say 'conformance list' (never 'suite', which already means the storage backends' suite), and give the per-list count recipe. Done: one use checks clean and Dynamics draws conformance-met with its two flows; a second use is refused as used-twice; the stand-in reads met 1, wanted 1, declared 2, unaccounted 0; an unlisted or never-run case puts every-case-run off; --budget equals the sensor's timeout. Files: the template and its stand-in lists, docs, tests/test_conformance_template.py (six tests). Budget: 0 net lines of Python, about 110 of YAML.

gaps.name: conformance-diagrams-list
gaps.title: ergostat's first conformance list: diagrams, five cases with checks that can fail
gaps.definition: Problem: the only count of what is drawn is a hand-kept '19 drawn today' (docs/DISCIPLINES.md:57) that nothing checks. Change: dev/conformance/diagrams.yaml (`list: diagrams`, each case citing its doc line in from:) with five cases: stock-and-flow, block-diagram and process-map (expected met; ergostat/web/server.py:460-491), service-map (no `map` view; docs/proposals/diagram-options.md:59-64) and sequence-diagram (docs/DISCIPLINES.md:36), both expected unmet and `asked: false` because the owner holds new diagrams. dev/conformance/checks/diagrams.py CASE builds the graph answer for examples/image-squeeze in-process through the function the /graph route calls (no server, no network) and exits 0 only when the answer holds what the case says (a node per stock and flow; a block per block and a junction per goal served; a node per state and a line per move on a small record it writes), 1 when the view or field is missing, 2 on its own error. Checks live outside tests/, so pytest never collects them. Done: the reader accepts the file with exactly these five cases; each check's result on main is in the record with any difference explained; each met check is shown able to fail (its view's builder patched to return no nodes exits 1); each runs under 60 s. Files: the list, the checks, tests/test_conformance_lists_ergostat.py (three tests). Budget: 150 net lines, dev/ counted.

gaps.name: conformance-model-formats-list

gaps.name: conformance-gap-requester
gaps.title: A program asks the factory for one gap per unmet, asked conformance case
gaps.definition: Problem: the factory never lets an AI change main directly; work arrives as gaps. The simplifier shows how a program asks for one (dev/bin/simplify.py:147-173): pool 1 under a lock, the open gaps read again under it, a definition written and gap.requested recorded with source. Change: new dev/bin/conformance.py. `request`: under run/conformance.lock read the open gaps and the case items, pick the unmet case with asked: true that has no gap in flight (by its `case` field) and has waited longest by its first case.unmet, write a definition in the house shape (the case's description and from as the problem; the change left to the implementor; a definition of done whose first point is '<check> exits 0 on main'; the check as the acceptance test; a budget of 300), and record gap.requested with source: conformance, case, title and definition through fac.add and fac.rel. `in-flight` prints the count of source: conformance gaps not merged, parked or closed. The gap kind in ergostat.yaml (:85) gains the relation `case: case`. Done: one gap naming the check and citing from; none while one is in flight; a case that is not asked, broken or withdrawn is never chosen; two runs at once ask at most once; the gap's item page shows the case as related; no machine or user names in the generated definition. Files: dev/bin/conformance.py, ergostat.yaml, tests/test_conformance_requester.py (five tests). Budget: 160 net lines, dev/ counted.
